To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the methionine enkaphalin (MENK), a naturally occurring neuropeptide that is involved in the control of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and immune system functions, is capable of augmenting tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha production and natural killer (NK) cell activity, and that the mechanism for these effects involves upregulation of the IL-12 p40 and p35 mRNA expression.

the use of the enkephalin analogs Met-enkephalin and Leu-enkephalin, and of the opioid antagonist naltrexone, can be useful to modulate the immune response and to improve the clinical outcome in patients with cancer.
the expression of methionine-enkephalin in the human endometrium is regulated during the menstrual cycle and that methionine-enkaphalin is able to modulate immune functions in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the endogenous opioid system in the immune system.
the role of the opioid peptide methionine encephalin (ME) on the immune system.
the development of novel, efficient and selective methods for the synthesis of biologically important compounds, including peptides, peptidomimetics, oligosaccharides and oligonucleotides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methionine enkphalin (MENK) peptide is a promising candidate for the treatment of cancer, especially in combination with the conventional therapies.
the use of the term "neuroimmunomodulation" is a misnomer.
the methionine encephalin is a potent immune enhancer, and it is a potent immune regulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient method for the synthesis of a library of peptides that are structurally related, but have different biological properties.
the expression of methionine enkaphalin in T cells is regulated by IL-2, and the enkephalin itself regulates the expression of IL-2, TNF-alpha and IFN-gamma.
the methionine encephalin (MENK) is a potent immune modulator that augments NK cell activity and TNF-alpha production by enhancing the expression of IL-12 p70 and IL-12p35 mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enkephalins, which are small peptides that bind to the opioid receptor mu (ORM), can have anti-tumor effects in a variety of tumor types.
we found that the combination of methionine-enkephalin and the TLR4 agonist LPS induced a significant up-regulation of TNF-alpha, NK cell activity, and IL-12p35 mRNA expression in the mouse spleen.

we have developed a novel method for the rapid synthesis of enkephalin peptides, and that the enkephalin analogs we have synthesized are more stable than the natural enkephalins and have greater potency as analgesics.
